```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(car)
library(tidyverse)
library(cluster)
library(ggplot2)
library(janitor)
```

```{r}
data <- read.csv("./src/Culminating_Activity/developer_survey.csv")
head(data)
```

# Load and Inspect Data
Apparently you don't have to convert categorical into numerical 
values in R, it just automatically labels them with the as.factor function

```{r}
sum(is.na(data$ai_tools_used))
head(data)
print("GLIMPSE")
glimpse(data)
print("SUMMARY")
summary(data)
```

# Feature Engineering
```{r}

# --- Stack breadth (simple numeric features) ---
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    n_languages  = str_count(languages_used,  ";") + 1,
    n_frameworks = str_count(frameworks_used, ";") + 1
  )

# --- Binary flags for top languages ---
# Find the most frequent languages across all respondents
top_languages <- data %>%
  pull(languages_used) %>%
  str_split(";") %>%
  unlist() %>%
  str_trim() %>%
  table() %>%
  sort(decreasing = TRUE) %>%
  head(10) %>%
  names()

cat("Top 10 languages:\n")
print(top_languages)

# Create one binary column per top language
for (lang in top_languages) {
  col_name <- paste0("lang_", janitor::make_clean_names(lang))
  data[[col_name]] <- as.integer(str_detect(data$languages_used, fixed(lang)))
}
```

# Preprocessing Data
```{r}

data_model <- data %>%
  filter(annual_salary_usd > 0) %>%           # Remove unreported/zero salaries
  mutate(
    log_salary = log(annual_salary_usd),       # Log-transform right-skewed target

    role    = factor(role),
    country = factor(country),

    # Ordered factor — preserves ordinal info in linear model
    experience_group = cut(years_of_experience,
                           breaks = c(-1, 1, 3, 7, 15, Inf),
                           labels = c("0-1", "2-3", "4-7", "8-15", "15+"))
  ) %>%
  select(
    log_salary, annual_salary_usd,
    role, years_of_experience, country,
    n_languages, n_frameworks,
    starts_with("lang_")
  ) %>%
  drop_na()

cat("Rows ready for modeling:", nrow(data_model), "\n")
glimpse(data_model)

```

# Model Fitting
```{r}
model <- lm(
  log_salary ~
    role +
    years_of_experience +
    country +
    n_languages +
    n_frameworks +
    lang_java_script +
    lang_python +
    lang_type_script +
    lang_sql +
    lang_java +
    lang_c +
    lang_html_css +
    lang_bash_shell,    
  data = data_model
)
```

# Model Summary
```{r}
summary(model)   # R², Adjusted R², p-values, t-stats per predictor

anova(model)     # F-tests — significance of each predictor GROUP

# Clean table: significant predictors only (p < 0.05)
tidy(model) %>%
  arrange(p.value) %>%
  mutate(significant = p.value < 0.05) %>%
  print(n = 60)

# Overall model fit
glance(model)
```

# Model Diagnostics
```{r}
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(model)
```
